# Dictionary in C# - A Crash Course

::: {.callout-note appearance="default" collapse="false"}
**Q:** Teach me a crash course about `Dictionary` and its methods (include how to create, index, safely get values, iterate over, etc.)
:::


## What is Dictionary?


```
Dictionary<TKey, TValue>
         ┌─────┴─────┐
         │           │
    Key Type    Value Type
         │           │
         └─────┬─────┘
               │
    ┌──────────┴───────────┐
    │  Key-Value Pairs     │
    │  ┌────────┬────────┐ │
    │  │  Key   │ Value  │ │
    │  ├────────┼────────┤ │
    │  │ "ABC"  │   123  │ │
    │  │ "DEF"  │   456  │ │
    │  │ "GHI"  │   789  │ │
    │  └────────┴────────┘ │
    └──────────────────────┘
```

`Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` is a **generic** collection that stores key-value pairs. Keys must be **unique** and **non-null**.


## Creating Dictionaries


### Basic Creation

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;

// 1. Empty dictionary
var emptyDict = new Dictionary<string, int>();

// 2. Collection initializer (most common)
var modalityCount = new Dictionary<string, int>
{
    { "CT", 150 },
    { "MR", 200 },
    { "CR", 300 }
};

// 3. Dictionary initializer (cleaner syntax - C# 6+)
var modalityCodes = new Dictionary<string, string>
{
    ["CT"] = "Computed Tomography",
    ["MR"] = "Magnetic Resonance",
    ["US"] = "Ultrasound"
};

// 4. With initial capacity (for performance)
var largeDict = new Dictionary<string, string>(1000);
```

**Comparison with Python:**
```python
# Python
modality_count = {"CT": 150, "MR": 200, "CR": 300}

# C#
var modalityCount = new Dictionary<string, int> { {"CT", 150}, {"MR", 200}, {"CR", 300} };
```


## Adding and Accessing Elements


```csharp
var studies = new Dictionary<string, string>();

// 1. Add using indexer (overwrites if key exists)
studies["1.2.840.113619.2.55"] = "CT Chest";
studies["1.2.840.113619.2.56"] = "MR Brain";

// 2. Add using Add method (throws if key exists)
try
{
    studies.Add("1.2.840.113619.2.55", "CT Abdomen"); // ❌ Throws ArgumentException
}
catch (ArgumentException)
{
    Console.WriteLine("Key already exists!");
}

// 3. TryAdd (returns false if key exists - C# 8+)
bool added = studies.TryAdd("1.2.840.113619.2.55", "CT Abdomen"); 
Console.WriteLine($"Added: {added}"); // False

// Accessing by key (throws if key doesn't exist)
string studyDesc = studies["1.2.840.113619.2.55"];
```


## Safely Getting Values


```csharp
var modalityNames = new Dictionary<string, string>
{
    ["CT"] = "Computed Tomography",
    ["MR"] = "Magnetic Resonance"
};

// ❌ UNSAFE: Direct access - throws KeyNotFoundException
// string name = modalityNames["XR"]; // Throws!

// ✅ Method 1: TryGetValue (RECOMMENDED)
if (modalityNames.TryGetValue("XR", out string? name))
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Found: {name}");
}
else
{
    Console.WriteLine("Key not found");
}

// ✅ Method 2: ContainsKey check
if (modalityNames.ContainsKey("CT"))
{
    string ctName = modalityNames["CT"];
    Console.WriteLine(ctName);
}

// ✅ Method 3: GetValueOrDefault (C# 9+)
string xrName = modalityNames.GetValueOrDefault("XR", "Unknown Modality");
Console.WriteLine(xrName); // "Unknown Modality"

// Without default value
string? mrName = modalityNames.GetValueOrDefault("MR");
Console.WriteLine(mrName); // "Magnetic Resonance"
```


## Iterating Over Dictionaries


```csharp
var patientData = new Dictionary<string, int>
{
    ["StudyCount"] = 5,
    ["SeriesCount"] = 15,
    ["ImageCount"] = 450
};

// 1. Iterate over KeyValuePair
foreach (KeyValuePair<string, int> kvp in patientData)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{kvp.Key}: {kvp.Value}");
}

// 2. Using var (cleaner)
foreach (var kvp in patientData)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{kvp.Key}: {kvp.Value}");
}

// 3. Deconstruction (C# 7+) - MOST COMMON
foreach (var (key, value) in patientData)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{key}: {value}");
}

// 4. Iterate over keys only
foreach (string key in patientData.Keys)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Key: {key}");
}

// 5. Iterate over values only
foreach (int value in patientData.Values)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"Value: {value}");
}
```


## Common Methods and Properties


```csharp
var dicomTags = new Dictionary<string, string>
{
    ["0010,0010"] = "Patient Name",
    ["0010,0020"] = "Patient ID",
    ["0008,0060"] = "Modality"
};

// Count
Console.WriteLine($"Total tags: {dicomTags.Count}"); // 3

// Clear all items
var temp = new Dictionary<string, string>(dicomTags);
temp.Clear();
Console.WriteLine($"After clear: {temp.Count}"); // 0

// Remove a key
bool removed = dicomTags.Remove("0010,0020");
Console.WriteLine($"Removed: {removed}"); // True

// ContainsKey
bool hasModality = dicomTags.ContainsKey("0008,0060"); // True

// ContainsValue (slower - O(n))
bool hasPatientName = dicomTags.ContainsValue("Patient Name"); // True

// Keys and Values collections
ICollection<string> keys = dicomTags.Keys;
ICollection<string> values = dicomTags.Values;
```


## LINQ with Dictionaries


```csharp
var studyCounts = new Dictionary<string, int>
{
    ["CT"] = 150,
    ["MR"] = 200,
    ["CR"] = 300,
    ["US"] = 50,
    ["XR"] = 400
};

// Filter
var highVolume = studyCounts
    .Where(kvp => kvp.Value > 100)
    .ToDictionary(kvp => kvp.Key, kvp => kvp.Value);

// Transform values
var doubled = studyCounts
    .ToDictionary(kvp => kvp.Key, kvp => kvp.Value * 2);

// Order by value
var sorted = studyCounts
    .OrderByDescending(kvp => kvp.Value)
    .ToList(); // Returns List<KeyValuePair>

foreach (var (modality, count) in sorted)
{
    Console.WriteLine($"{modality}: {count}");
}

// Sum all values
int total = studyCounts.Values.Sum();

// Get max value
int max = studyCounts.Values.Max();

// Get key with max value
string topModality = studyCounts
    .OrderByDescending(kvp => kvp.Value)
    .First()
    .Key;
```


## Dictionary vs Other Collections


```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│            Collection Type Comparison                    │
├────────────────┬──────────────┬─────────────────────────┤
│ Type           │ Access       │ Use Case                 │
├────────────────┼──────────────┼─────────────────────────┤
│ Dictionary     │ O(1) by key  │ Key-value lookups        │
│ List           │ O(1) by idx  │ Ordered collection       │
│ HashSet        │ O(1)         │ Unique values only       │
│ SortedDict     │ O(log n)     │ Sorted key-value pairs   │
└────────────────┴──────────────┴─────────────────────────┘
```


## Practical Example: DICOM Study Manager


```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Linq;

class Program
{
    static void Main()
    {
        // Create a dictionary to map Study Instance UID to Study Description
        var studies = new Dictionary<string, string>
        {
            ["1.2.840.113619.2.55.1.1"] = "CT Chest with Contrast",
            ["1.2.840.113619.2.55.1.2"] = "MR Brain without Contrast",
            ["1.2.840.113619.2.55.1.3"] = "CR Chest PA and Lateral"
        };

        // Safe access with TryGetValue
        string targetUid = "1.2.840.113619.2.55.1.2";
        if (studies.TryGetValue(targetUid, out string? description))
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"Found study: {description}");
        }

        Console.WriteLine("\nAll Studies:");
        Console.WriteLine("─────────────");
        
        // Iterate with deconstruction
        foreach (var (uid, desc) in studies)
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"UID: {uid}");
            Console.WriteLine($"Description: {desc}\n");
        }

        // Count studies by modality
        var modalityCounts = new Dictionary<string, int>();
        
        foreach (var desc in studies.Values)
        {
            string modality = desc.Split(' ')[0]; // Get first word
            
            if (modalityCounts.ContainsKey(modality))
            {
                modalityCounts[modality]++;
            }
            else
            {
                modalityCounts[modality] = 1;
            }
        }

        Console.WriteLine("Modality Counts:");
        Console.WriteLine("────────────────");
        
        foreach (var (modality, count) in modalityCounts.OrderByDescending(x => x.Count))
        {
            Console.WriteLine($"{modality}: {count}");
        }
    }
}
```

**Output:**
```
Found study: MR Brain without Contrast

All Studies:
─────────────
UID: 1.2.840.113619.2.55.1.1
Description: CT Chest with Contrast

UID: 1.2.840.113619.2.55.1.2
Description: MR Brain without Contrast

UID: 1.2.840.113619.2.55.1.3
Description: CR Chest PA and Lateral

Modality Counts:
────────────────
CT: 1
MR: 1
CR: 1
```


## Key Differences from Python


| Feature | Python | C# |
|---------|--------|-----|
| Access missing key | Returns `None` or raises `KeyError` | Throws `KeyNotFoundException` |
| Safe access | `.get(key, default)` | `.TryGetValue(key, out value)` |
| Check existence | `key in dict` | `.ContainsKey(key)` |
| Type safety | Dynamic | Strongly typed: `Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` |
| Declaration | `dict = {}` | `new Dictionary<string, int>()` |


## Important Notes


1. **Keys must be immutable** - strings, numbers, enums are good. Custom objects must properly implement `GetHashCode()` and `Equals()`

2. **Null keys not allowed** - Unlike Python, you cannot use `null` as a key

3. **Value types** - If using nullable value types, declare as `Dictionary<string, int?>`

4. **Thread safety** - `Dictionary` is NOT thread-safe. Use `ConcurrentDictionary` for multi-threaded scenarios

5. **Performance** - Dictionary operations are O(1) average case, but can degrade to O(n) with poor hash functions
